perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works as a construction worker at the same company where Elizabeth is the receptionist; they have a friendly but professional colleague relationship.
- Over the past few days, he observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him.
- He suspected she might be upset with him, possibly due to a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake he made.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had upset her. He heard her say no, not at all, and that she was dealing with personal stuff; she apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, he heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses; he perceived them as quite severe.
- He believed professional help might benefit her, but worried about offending her.
- He told her he appreciated her sharing, asked if she had considered talking to a professional, and suggested an external perspective could help.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that, he noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. He heard her say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- After their last conversation, he observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He intended to maintain this supportive relationship.
- He told her he was glad they could talk and that he was always available to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
